# Audit child screens cannot verify execution-dependent ACs (no green-run evidence in child prompts)

## Problem statement

The audit runner resolves verified green-run evidence for the audited HEAD and injects it
as an evidence block (operator attestation, AUTO-VERIFIED GREEN RUN from the cached
full-suite run, or TEST-SKILL GREEN RUN from an executed run) into the **parent** Phase-1
screen and into **all Phase-2** prompts — but **not** into either child Phase-1 screen. A
child AC that is execution-dependent ("All new tests run through the test skill and collect
cleanly", "full suite passes") is therefore scored `partial` by the child screen even when a
green full-suite run at the same HEAD exists and is already consumed for the parent's own
equivalent AC, leaving the parent permanently un-closable.

## Goal

As an auditor, I need a child work item's execution-dependent ACs judged on the same verified
green-run evidence the parent gets, so that delivered children stop being scored `partial` for
missing prompt content and their parent epic can be closed.

## Impact / users

- **Release operators / auditors** running `audit_runner.py` on multi-child items: a parent
  with one execution-dependent child AC can never reach `Ready to close: Yes`; each re-audit
  re-demotes the child out of `in_review` (10 children demoted in the reported session, two
  of which had been `Ready to close: Yes`), churning delivered work.
- **Implementing agents**: an already-delivered child stays "not ready" for a reason that is
  an evidence-plumbing gap, not a code defect.

Reported instance (2026-10-25, `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`, resident-prefix admission epic):
child `LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H` AC9 — "All new tests run through the test skill (`/skill:test`)
and collect cleanly with the rest of `proxy/tests`" — was scored `partial` with the evidence
"… actual run-through of /skill:test and clean collection with the rest of proxy/tests is an
execution result not verifiable under this read-only audit (no pytest run performed)". Every
parent AC was `met`/`adjusted`, code quality was clean, and a green full-suite run existed at
the same HEAD (`3c9b8e34`, `3c5413ac`) and *was* consumed for the parent's AC9.

Example user stories:

- "As an auditor, when a green full-suite run exists at the audited HEAD, I want a child's
  execution-dependent AC to be judged on that evidence — not on a prompt that never mentions
  it — so the epic can close."
- "As a release operator, I want re-audits to stop demoting delivered children for an
  evidence-plumbing gap."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — evidence reaches child screens.** The child Phase-1 screens receive the same
   verified green-run evidence block (and the execution-dependent AC guidance it carries)
   that the parent Phase-1 screen receives, whenever such evidence exists at the audited
   HEAD. Applies to **both** child Phase-1 paths: the per-child screen
   (`_phase1_review_child_acs`) and the opt-in batched screen
   (`_phase1_review_children_batched`, `--batch-phase1` / `AUDIT_PHASE1_BATCH`), and to every
   call site (the `_phase_children` pass-through path, the gap-mapped auto-trigger loop, and
   the budget-exceeded re-audit path).
2. **AC2 — no false `partial`.** A child AC that is execution-dependent is marked `met` when
   the cached full-suite run at the audited HEAD is green with `scope == "full"` (or an
   accepted operator attestation / executed test-skill run exists), and `partial` — with the
   existing diagnostic wording — only when no such evidence exists at that HEAD.
3. **AC3 — regression test.** A test asserts that each child Phase-1 prompt (single-child and
   batched) contains the green-run evidence text when the evidence is green at HEAD, that the
   prompt is unchanged when no evidence exists, and that the child screen's verdict path does
   not degrade to `partial` for a `met` verdict returned against that evidence.
4. **AC4 — no scope widening.** The parent/child AC rules, model selection and JSON contract
   are otherwise unchanged; child screens still never execute the suite themselves (the
   evidence block explicitly forbids it); `partial`-on-missing-verdict semantics and the
   capped-screen quarantine behaviour are untouched.

Standard criteria for every item:

5. New and changed tests are run through the test skill (`/skill:test`) and collect cleanly
   with the rest of the audit skill's suite.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
   the audit skill's `SKILL.md`, and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (both currently say
   the green-run block goes into the "Phase 1 parent prompt and ALL Phase 2 prompts").
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Existing state (code map — as inspected at intake)

Repository: the audit skill's source of truth is **`~/projects/SorraAgents`**; `~/.pi/agent/skills`
is a symlink to `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill`. Line numbers below are from
`~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` at intake time.

- **Evidence blocks exist and are already parent/Phase-2-aware:**
  - `_green_run_prompt_block(sha)` — operator attestation block ("GREEN-RUN ATTESTATION").
  - `_auto_green_run_prompt_block(sha)` — cached full-suite block ("AUTO-VERIFIED GREEN RUN"),
    used only when the cached entry's scope is `full`.
  - `_test_skill_run_prompt_block(sha)` — executed-suite block ("TEST-SKILL GREEN RUN").
  - Block selection happens once per run (`_resolve_green_run_attestation` + the
    cache/auto-execute path) and is stored on `ctx.green_run_block`.
- **Where the block is injected today:** parent Phase-1 screen
  (`_phase1_parent_screening`, injection at the `{_SCANNING_BLOCK}` splice ~line 11768);
  parent Phase-2 deep prompt; child Phase-2 deep prompt (`_run_child_phase2_deep_analysis`,
  ~line 8231); Phase-2 batch prompt (~line 8528); and the parent branch of
  `_run_phase2_deep_analysis` (~line 8791).
- **Where it is absent today (the defect):**
  - `_phase1_review_child_acs` (child Phase-1 screen, `def` at ~line 7550, prompt splicing
    `_SCANNING_BLOCK` at ~line 7606) — has **no** `green_run_block` parameter and never
    injects the block.
  - `_phase1_review_children_batched` (batched child Phase-1 screen, `def` at ~line 7364,
    splice at ~line 7441) — same gap.
  - Call sites that would thread the block: `_phase_children` pass-through path (~12189
    batched / ~12202 threaded / ~12217 sequential), the gap-mapped auto-trigger loop
    (~12733 / ~12746 / ~12761), and the budget-exceeded re-audit path (~11609). `_phase_children`
    already binds `green_run_block = ctx.green_run_block` (~11942), so the value is in scope.
- **Docs that state the current (now-known-wrong) contract:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~lines
  332 and 334: "injects … into the Phase 1 parent prompt and ALL Phase 2 prompts") and
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (~lines 685 and 705, same claim).
- **Tests that will grow:** `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_green_run.py`
  (`TestGreenRunPromptInjection` already asserts the block's presence in the parent Phase-1
  and every Phase-2 prompt, and its absence with no attestation) — the natural home for the
  child-screen assertions; `tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` and
  `tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` provide the child fixtures/helpers.

## Desired change

Thread the resolved green-run evidence block into both child Phase-1 screen prompts (and
their call sites), exactly as the parent screen and the Phase-2 prompts already receive it,
and cover the new contract with prompt-level regression tests plus doc updates.

- Add a `green_run_block: str | None = None` keyword parameter to
  `_phase1_review_child_acs` and `_phase1_review_children_batched`, splicing
  `f"{green_run_block or ''}"` immediately after `_SCANNING_BLOCK` (mirroring the parent and
  Phase-2 prompt build order) so an absent block leaves the prompt byte-identical.
- Pass `green_run_block=green_run_block` (from `ctx.green_run_block`) at all five child-screen
  call sites, including the sequential, threaded and batched dispatch branches.
- Preserve in-main-slot emission: the emitted `phase1_child_screen` prompt must carry the same
  block, since it is the prompt the main session executes.
- No change to verdict normalisation, the JSON contract, the capped-screen quarantine, or the
  `partial`-when-no-verdict rule.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo (documented precedent):** the code lives in `~/projects/SorraAgents`
  (`skill/audit/…`) while the work item is tracked in the **llm** worklog — precedent:
  `LP-0MSQ32S2M001EA74` / `LP-0MSQ79OBO0019CNP` ("code in ~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/,
  item tracked in llm worklog"). Implementation must commit and push in **SorraAgents**
  (`dev`), with the commit hash recorded on this item.
- **Read-only audit mandate:** child screens must still never execute the suite; the injected
  block itself states the runner manages execution.
- **Fail-closed evidence:** no evidence at HEAD ⇒ no block ⇒ execution-dependent child ACs
  stay `partial` (never a fabricated `met`).
- **No scope widening (AC4):** do not change prompt rules, models, thresholds or the JSON
  contract; do not add new evidence sources.
- **Opt-in surfaces preserved:** `--batch-phase1` stays opt-in and in-main-slot mode stays
  sequential (`--child-in-main-slot`); the block must reach both.
- **Test execution policy:** agent test runs go through the test skill (`/skill:test`), never
  ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Key Files

- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — add the `green_run_block`
  parameter and prompt splice to `_phase1_review_child_acs` (~7550) and
  `_phase1_review_children_batched` (~7364); thread the block at the five child-screen call
  sites (~11609, ~12189/12202/12217, ~12733/12746/12761).
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_green_run.py` — new prompt
  assertions for the child Phase-1 screens (present with evidence, absent without; batched and
  single-child), plus the non-degradation assertion for AC2/AC3.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/SKILL.md` — correct the two "Phase 1 parent prompt and
  ALL Phase 2 prompts" claims to include the child Phase-1 screens.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — same correction in the
  operator-attestation (~685) and automatic-verification / F3 (~705) sections.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — child fixtures
  (existing helper `_phase1_child`) reused by the new tests if a batched-path fixture is
  cleaner there.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` — resident-prefix admission / session tenancy epic that surfaced the
  defect (its AC9 is `met` off the same green run the child's AC9 was denied).
- `LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H` — the child whose execution-dependent AC was scored `partial`.
- `SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W` / `SA-0MSJELL44009XYIL` — automatic full-suite verification and the
  audit's 24h green-evidence acceptance window.
- `SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC` — `scope == "full"` cache filtering (a `changed`-scope entry is a miss,
  never evidence) — the rule AC2 depends on.
- `SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP` — F3 default auto-execution (green executed run → TEST-SKILL GREEN RUN block).
- `SA-0MVI6VRJT005M650` — opt-in batched Phase-1 child screening (`_phase1_review_children_batched`).
- `SA-0MVJ3Q662006RDJR` — parent Phase-1 budget/batching/JSON robustness (parent-side twin of
  this gap).
- `SA-0MVI3608M0080QLW` / `SA-0MU32TE120012T49` — child-screen budget/quarantine and the
  child-audit execution contract (unchanged by this item — AC4).
- `LP-0MSQ32S2M001EA74` / `LP-0MSQ79OBO0019CNP` — cross-repo precedent for audit-runner work
  tracked in the llm worklog with code in SorraAgents.
- **Note on the automated report below:** its repository-file matches are not informative
  for this item — the audit skill's code lives in `~/projects/SorraAgents`, so keyword hits in
  this (llm) checkout are unrelated data/rendered-prompt artefacts. The related *work items*
  it lists (per-call budget, ruff findings, slot-aware child-call concurrency) are audit-runner
  siblings on the same code path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — the observed case may have a second contributing cause.** The persisted child
  report for `LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H` reads like a standalone child audit, and the auto-triggered
  child-audit subprocess threads `--run-tests` but **not** `--green-run`/`AUDIT_GREEN_RUN`
  into the child process (~12318). If the child report was produced by such a subprocess, the
  missing block in the *in-process* child screen is necessary but may not be sufficient for
  that historical instance. **Mitigation:** the implementation verifies the fix by asserting
  the child prompt carries the block, and (out of scope for this item, AC4) records the
  `--green-run` non-propagation to child audit subprocesses as a **discovered follow-up**
  work item if it can still produce a false `partial` when no cache entry exists.
- **Assumption — evidence resolution is already correct.** The runner decides *whether*
  evidence exists before any prompt is built; this item only fixes prompt plumbing, so the
  `scope == "full"` filter, the 24h window and the fail-closed path need no change (AC4).
- **Assumption — prompt-level fix is the intended mechanism.** AC2's "marked `met`" is
  achieved the same way it is for the parent: the evidence block authorises the model to mark
  execution-dependent criteria met. No post-processing override of child verdicts is added
  (that would violate AC4).
- **Assumption — cross-repo delivery is acceptable** (precedent above); the item stays in the
  llm worklog and the SorraAgents commit is recorded on it.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the `--green-run` non-propagation above, and any wish to auto-mark
  child ACs programmatically, are recorded as linked follow-ups, not absorbed here.
- **Risk — prompt-size drift:** the block adds ~1 short paragraph per child screen. In the
  batched path it is emitted once per call (not per child), so prompt growth is bounded;
  the batched prompt remains within the child-screen budget (`AUDIT_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT`),
  and a capped screen keeps its quarantine behaviour.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does intake need a new interview round for this item?**
  — Answer (Map, agent): No. The seed context already states a problem, an observed instance
  with evidence, four testable ACs and a no-scope-widening constraint; the open points are
  answerable from the repository. Source: `/skill:intake LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6`; research: the
  audit skill source inspected at `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
  (block builders at ~2815/2908/3123; parent Phase-1 splice ~11768; Phase-2 splices ~8231/
  8528/8791; child Phase-1 `def`s at ~7550/7364 with no `green_run_block` parameter).
- **Q: Which repository owns the fix, given the item is in the llm worklog?**
  — Answer (Map, agent): `~/projects/SorraAgents` (`skill/audit/`), which is the source of
  truth behind the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink. Evidence: `readlink -f ~/.pi/agent/skills/audit`
  → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit`; `/home/rgardler/projects/llm` has no
  `skill/` tree. Precedent: closed item `LP-0MSQ32S2M001EA74` comment "Cross-repo: code in
  ~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/, item tracked in llm worklog".
- **Q: Is any completed item already satisfying these ACs (duplicate check)?**

  contract) are all completed and none injects the green-run evidence block into child
  Phase-1 prompts. Recorded as a comment on this item ("Duplicate check performed — no

- **Q: Should the fix also propagate `--green-run` into auto-triggered child audit

## Goal

As an operator I need `llama_process_rss_bytes` / `llama_model_rss_bytes` to
report real memory figures, so memory pressure on the llama-server process can be
alerted on instead of being permanently invisible.

## Context

Discovered while resolving the dead alert groups in LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48. The
proxy publishes both RSS gauges as **0** on every scrape:

```
llama_process_rss_bytes 0.0
llama_model_rss_bytes{model="Qwen3"} 0.0        # and every other model label
```

Original diagnosis: `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (`/admin/metrics`) only reads RSS
when it holds a live host process handle:

```python
if 'psutil' in dir(srv) and srv.psutil and srv.llama_process is not None:
    pid = getattr(srv.llama_process, 'pid', None)
    ...
    process_rss = getattr(mem, 'rss', None)
```

llama-server can run inside a **podman container**
(`scripts/podman_start_llama.sh`, container `${PODMAN_LC_CONTAINER:-llama}`), so
`srv.llama_process` is the host-side `podman exec` wrapper (or `None`),
`process_rss` stays `None`, and `metrics.update_metrics(None, models)` sets
`llama_process_rss_bytes = 0` and zeroes every `llama_model_rss_bytes` label. The
status/`/admin/metrics` endpoint likewise reports `process_rss_bytes: null`.

### Root-cause correction (verified live, 2026-10-26)

The container is **not** the only failure mode. On this host llama-server runs
host-direct (no podman containers were running) and the gauges are still 0:

- `ps -eo pid,rss,cmd` showed a host `llama-server` router (`rss` ≈ 0.34 GB) with
  a model child process holding ≈ 45 GB — **router-mode model memory lives in
  child processes, not in the top-level process**. Reading only
  `llama_process.pid` therefore under-reports by ~99% even when a pid is
  available.
- `curl localhost:8000/admin/metrics` returned `process_rss_bytes: null` although
  `llama_server_running: true`: the proxy had restarted ~2 h earlier and
  **adopted** the 3-day-old server via `_AdoptedLlamaProcess`, whose sentinel
  carries `pid = 0` (`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`), so `if pid:` is false.
- `/metrics` is served from the already-set gauges
  (`metrics.generate_metrics_payload()`), while `metrics.update_metrics()` has a
  single caller — the `/admin/metrics` handler. Prometheus scrapes `/metrics`
  every 15 s (`monitoring/prometheus.yml`), so the series are only refreshed when
  something separately polls `/admin/metrics`; otherwise they stay at their
  registered 0.
- llama.cpp's own `/metrics` exposes **no** RSS/memory series (checked against a
  live server), so the container/proc/cgroup view is the only source of truth.
- Both runtime paths must keep working: `proxy/config.yaml` sets
  `llama_start_script: start-llama.sh` with `llama_allow_host_fallback: true`, and
  the container path (`scripts/podman_start_llama.sh`) is the documented default
  for container-managed deployments. The fix is **additive**: keep the existing
  host-pid path.

Consequence: the `LlamaMemoryHighWarning` / `LlamaMemoryHighCritical` rules
(75% / 90% of 90 GB on `llama_process_rss_bytes`) could never fire, so they were
deleted in LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48 and GPU memory pressure is now alerted on
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes` instead. That covers the GPU-visible pool, but the proxy's
own RSS (and the per-model attribution) is still unmeasured, and the existing
`monitoring/llama_memory_alerts.yaml` documentation references disappeared with
the rules.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/admin/metrics` RSS read (host-pid only) and `/metrics` handler
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — `update_metrics()` gauges and the zero-on-`None` behaviour
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `_AdoptedLlamaProcess` sentinel (`pid = 0`) and `start_llama_server()`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — existing router child-port discovery (reusable for per-model attribution)
- `scripts/podman_start_llama.sh` — container name and `podman exec` wrapper
- `proxy/tests/test_metrics.py` — metric unit tests
- `proxy/tests/test_observability_regression.py` — `/metrics` payload regression guard
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` / `REQUIRED_RULE_FILES` guards
- `monitoring/prometheus.yml` — scrape path (`/metrics`) and `rule_files`
- `monitoring/gpu_memory_alerts.yaml` — existing GTT memory-pressure coverage
- `monitoring/llama_memory_alerts.yaml` — removed file, to be restored if AC5 restores the alert

## Acceptance criteria

1. `llama_process_rss_bytes` returns a non-zero value within 5% of the
   llama-server's actual resident memory — `podman stats --no-stream` /
   cgroup `memory.current` for the container, or the summed RSS of the
   llama-server process tree on the host — while a model is loaded, and it stays
   fresh when only `/metrics` is scraped (Prometheus does not call
   `/admin/metrics`).
2. `llama_model_rss_bytes{model=...}` attributes memory per loaded model with the
   documented heuristic (equal split or a better measure), and the labelled
   values sum to within ~10% of `llama_process_rss_bytes`.
3. The value is obtained without requiring a host-side process handle when
   llama-server runs in podman (e.g. resolve the container via
   `podman inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}'` plus its cgroup `memory.current`, or
   `podman inspect`/`podman stats`), and the resolution chain covers the
   adopted-server case (`_AdoptedLlamaProcess` has `pid = 0`) and the router-child
   case (model memory held by child processes). It degrades safely when the
   runtime is unavailable: the scrape still succeeds and the failure is logged
   once, not per scrape.
4. A test asserts a non-zero RSS is published for a mocked container-backed
   backend, and that the RSS path fails soft (still serves `/metrics`) when the
   container runtime lookup raises.
5. A memory-pressure alert on the now-working series is restored (or a decision
   is recorded that GTT coverage in `gpu_memory_alerts.yaml` is sufficient). If
   the alert is restored, `llama_process_rss_bytes` is removed from
   `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`, the
   rule file is registered in `monitoring/prometheus.yml` `rule_files` (and in
   `REQUIRED_RULE_FILES`), and the "removed because the series is 0" comment in
   `prometheus.yml` is updated.

## Verification

- `curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep llama_process_rss_bytes` — non-zero,
  refreshed between two consecutive 15 s scrapes with no `/admin/metrics` poll.
- `curl -s localhost:8000/admin/metrics | jq .process_rss_bytes` — non-null and
  matching the gauge.
- Host-direct: compare with `ps -o rss= -p <router pid>` plus its model children.
- Container: compare with `podman stats --no-stream llama` and
  `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/.../libpod-*.scope/memory.current`.
- Runtime absent/erroring: `/metrics` still returns 200 and the warning appears
  once in the proxy log.

## Notes

- Not blocking LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; the dead rules were removed and GTT coverage
  added there, so no alert is silently dead in the meantime.
- Related: LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT (monitoring tree), LP-0MQR554O60033BGF (Grafana,
  which would consume these series).
- Implement test-first: extend `proxy/tests/test_metrics.py` /
  `test_observability_regression.py` before touching the handler.
- Observed-but-out-of-scope: `loaded_models` on `/health` and `/admin/metrics`
  currently lists every alias in the preset (~15 labels) rather than only the
  loaded models, so equal-split attribution is arithmetically correct but

# Skill-suite tests are invisible to the repo full-suite gate

## Goal (headline)

The dev-push full-suite gate must execute the project-local skill tests under
`.pi/skills/*/tests` (529 tests today), so a regression in the observability the
audit and the 05:00 cron depend on can no longer pass the gate silently.

> **Status: DECIDED — blocked-by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB.** Decision: option 3
> (upstream fix in the test skill, SorraAgents), coverage breadth **all**
> `.pi/skills/*/tests` directories. The llm repo is intentionally **not**
> configured with a local pin (see Constraints); enforcement arrives when the
> upstream item ships. Work on this item starts only after that.

**Headline for the report:** the repo's dev-push full-suite gate only ever
collects `tests/` and `proxy/` (5 264 tests), because pytest's default
`norecursedirs` includes `.*` and therefore prunes `.pi/`; the 529 real, ~6 s
`proxy-usage-analysis` skill tests were enforced by nothing. The fix is now owned
upstream (SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB); this item proves the enforcement, publishes the
split counts, keeps the convention path active, and guards against drift.

## Producer decision (AC1)

Decision recorded 2026-10-27 (intake round 1 answers):

| Question | Answer | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Enforcement option | **Option 3 — upstream generic fix in the test skill (`run_tests.py` `full_suite_commands`), tracked as SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** | One resolution rule serves every project; no repo-local pin to maintain. Producer constraint: projects can supply local test-skill configuration, so a pinned `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` must stay authoritative (returned verbatim, gap surfaced as a notice) — captured as D3/AC3 on the upstream item. |
| Coverage breadth (Q2) | **All** `.pi/skills/*/tests` directories | Identical cost today (only one skill ships tests) and future skill suites are covered without another change. |

Rejected alternatives, for the record:

- **Option 1 — `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` with a second pytest
  command.** Would give the same coverage, but setting `suiteCommands` makes
  `changed_scope_commands()` return `None` (`run_tests.py:645`), so every
  `implement.py finish` falls back to the **full** suite (~302 s instead of a
  changed subset) — a silent local-loop regression (AC4).
- **Option 2 — root `pytest.ini` with `testpaths = . .pi/skills/*/tests`.**
  Works (testpaths entries are pytest initial paths and bypass `norecursedirs`)
  and keeps the finish loop fast, but it is a per-repo workaround that every
  project with local skills would have to repeat.
- **Option 4 — document the gap.** Leaves 529 tests unenforced.

## Problem statement

`run_tests.py --scope full` resolves the suite to a single canonical command,
`pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`, executed from the repo root. pytest's
default `norecursedirs` (`*.egg .* _darcs build CVS dist node_modules venv`)
prunes every dot-directory, so `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` is never
collected. Adding 10 tests there left the published full-suite count unchanged at
**5 264 passed**, while running that directory explicitly collects **529 passed**
in roughly 6 s. Those 529 tests are the only automated guard on
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — the report the
`audit` skill and the daily 05:00 cron read.

## Users and user stories

- **Implementing agent** — "As an agent changing the usage-analysis parser, I want
  the push gate to refuse my change when a skill test breaks, so I do not ship a
  silently wrong report."
- **Producer / audit** — "As the audit, I want the published full-suite number to
  provably include the skill tests, so 'green' means the same thing in every
  consumer."
- **Operator** — "As the operator, I want the gate cost to stay predictable
  (about +6 s cold) and the local `implement.py finish` loop to stay fast."

## Measured evidence

Recorded 2026-10-25 by LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G, re-verified for this brief on the
current tree:

| Observation | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Gate command | `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings` (scope `full`) | `.worklog/cache/*/metadata.json` |
| Full-suite total before/after adding 10 skill tests | **5 264 passed / 5 264 passed** (unchanged) | item comment, LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G |
| `pytest .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` | **529 passed**, ~6 s | item comment, LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G |
| Skill test modules | 6 `test_*.py` + `conftest.py` + `fixtures.py` + `__init__.py`, all git-tracked | `git ls-files .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` |
| Cold full suite on this host | ~302 s | `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` |
| Per-command timeout | 1800 s | `.pi/test-config.json` |
| pytest version | 9.0.3 | host interpreter |

Mechanism, confirmed against the installed pytest source
(`_pytest/main.py:425` `pytest_ignore_collect`, `Dir.collect` at :552): the
`norecursedirs` check is skipped for *initial paths* (paths given on the command
line or via `testpaths`), which is exactly why the explicit run collects the 529
tests while the recursive run cannot see them. The upstream fix exploits this by
emitting the skill directories as an explicit pytest initial path.

## Existing state

- `.pi/test-config.json` contains only `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1800}` — no
  `suiteCommands`, no `groups`. This is deliberate: it keeps the convention
  detection path active so the upstream rule applies here.
- There is **no** root `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` / `setup.cfg` / `tox.ini`,
  so the gate runs with rootdir = repo root and no ini file; recursion from the
  root picks up `tests/` and all of `proxy/` (including
  `proxy/proxy/test_home_page.py`) → 5 264 tests.
- `proxy/pytest.ini` registers the proxy markers (`slow`, `live`,
  `live_port_kill`, …); it is only loaded when pytest is invoked from `proxy/`,
  not by the root gate run.
- Only one of the three project-local skills ships tests
  (`proxy-usage-analysis`); `proxy-log-debug` and `start-proxy` have none. Its
  `tests/conftest.py` puts `../scripts` on `sys.path`, so collection works from
  any cwd inside the repo.
- `.githooks/pre-push` delegates suite resolution to `run_tests.py` (repo-local
  first, then the global install) and runs `--scope full`; the audit skill's F3
  check resolves the same commands through `full_suite_commands()`.
- Upstream work item **SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (SorraAgents) carries the resolution
  change, its precedence rules (pinned `suiteCommands` verbatim + notice,
  `testpaths`/`addopts` de-duplication, groups/types untouched) and its own tests
  and docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Decision recorded.** ✅ Recorded above (option 3 + all skill test
  dirs), with the rejected alternatives and their runtime-cost rationale, and
  mirrored to the upstream item.
- **AC2 — Enforcement proven end-to-end.** After SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB ships and
  its runner is installed, add a deliberately failing test under
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` on a scratch branch, observe the push
  to `dev` being **refused** by the gate, then remove the test and confirm green.
  Record the gate output excerpt (naming the skill-test command) in a comment.
- **AC3 — Counts published separately.** Publish the repo-test count, the
  skill-test count and the combined total as three distinct numbers in a
  work-item comment and in `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`, so the surfaces can never be
  conflated again.
- **AC4 — No finish-gate regression.** `implement.py finish`'s change-scope
  selection still returns a subset command (not a full-suite fallback) for a
  representative change, and the measured cold-gate runtime after the change is
  documented (expected ~302 s + ~6 s).
- **AC5 — Drift guard.** An automated test in `tests/` asserts that the resolved
  full-suite command set includes a command targeting
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` (importing the installed
  `run_tests.py` through its resolved path and calling `full_suite_commands()` —
  no nested suite execution), so a future configuration or resolution change
  cannot silently re-blind the gate.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` documents that the gate covers
  repo tests *and* project-local skill tests, the split counts, the measured
  runtime, and the rule that this repo must not pin `suiteCommands` (doing so
  would drop the skill tests until they are listed explicitly). Affected code
  comments updated.
- **AC7 — Full suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the change
  applied — repo tests plus the skill tests, no regressions, no collection
  errors, and no duplicate collection.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB.** Do not implement a repo-local workaround
  (no `suiteCommands`, no root `pytest.ini` `testpaths`) — the decision is
  explicitly the upstream route.
- **Project-local test-skill configuration stays authoritative.** llm's
  `.pi/test-config.json` keeps only `timeoutPerCommand`. Adding `suiteCommands`
  here would make the skill tests silently drop out again (the pinned list wins
  by design) and would also disable changed-scope selection.
- **Repository boundary.** No edits to the global skill install
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills`) or to `skill/` from this repo; the code change belongs
  to SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB.
- **Single source of truth.** Suite-command resolution stays in `run_tests.py`;
  do not fork it inside `.githooks/pre-push`.
- **Cost budget.** Skill tests add ~6 s to a ~302 s cold gate; `timeoutPerCommand`
  stays 1800.
- UK English in all written output.

## Desired change

No product-code change in this repo. After the upstream item ships: verify
enforcement (AC2), publish the three counts (AC3), confirm the finish loop is
unchanged (AC4), add the drift-guard test (AC5), update
`docs/dev/git-hooks.md` (AC6), and run the full suite (AC7).

- `.githooks/pre-push` — expected **unchanged**.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` — unchanged (the 529 tests being

- Upstream (not edited here): SorraAgents `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`,

  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB lands with the precedence rules intact

- **Assumption:** the 5 264 / 529 numbers from LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G still hold;

- **Scope-creep risk:** extending changed-scope selection so skill tests run for

- Any repo-local test configuration workaround (see Constraints).
- Making the changed-scope gate select skill tests for edits to skill scripts

# Intake Brief — In-request local re-dispatch after a prefill-deadline cancellation re-arms the lease and holds the gate ~6 min

## Problem statement

A local dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` (120 s) does not reliably
end the session's claim on the local gate: the same session immediately re-dispatches
local and acquires a **fresh dispatch lease**, whose record stays `active` without
producing a first byte and is released only by the no-progress watchdog ~308 s later.
Other sessions are denied (`local_dispatch_denied`, `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue
reason=local_lease_active`) for 311–322 s each — beyond the epic's <=5 min per-hold bound
(LP-0MVKN9IRP003XJH6 AC1) and the only remaining `wedge_denials > 0` signal
(`ac1.wedge_denials: 3` in the 2026-10-25 21:19 → 2026-10-26 21:19 window, verified
`ac1.verdict_met: false`).

## Users / stakeholders

- **Operator** (user story): *"As an operator, I want a local dispatch cancelled by the
  prefill deadline to stop holding the local dispatch gate, so the next session is not
  denied for longer than the epic's <=5 min bound."*
- **Sessions sharing the local gateway**: during the hold they are forced remote
  (3 refusals in this incident, 311–322 s each; the 2026-10-23 incident was ~3 orders
  of magnitude larger and unbounded).

## Mechanism decision (intake determination, 2026-10-26 — log `proxy.log.2026-10-26_131429`)

**Candidate (a) is confirmed; candidate (b) is refuted as the operative mechanism:**

1. `[local] POST` fires **147–150 ms after** each `lease_released reason=prefill_deadline`
   (10:39:36,396 → 10:39:36,546; 10:41:36,629 → 10:41:36,776) — a fresh local dispatch
   in the same request/retry window, so a *new* record is acquired **after** the release.
2. `_extend_lease_during_prefill` only mutates an **existing active** record, yet
   `lease_extended_during_prefill ... in_flight=True` resumes at 10:41:46, exactly 10 s
   after the 10:41:36 release — proving a fresh **active** record exists post-release
   (mechanism (b) — release removing a differently-keyed record — would leave no record
   for the extension path to touch; the release path only logs `lease_released` when it
   actually removed a record).
3. The hold chain: record acquired ~10:44:25 (same session re-acquisition — always
   permitted by `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`): no extensions after 10:44:18, denials at
   10:46:57/10:47:08 with `owner=01a177c6…`, released 10:47:33 by
   `reason=no_progress_watchdog` (≈10:44:25 + 180 s watchdog + 10 s sweep) ≈ **308 s
   unproductive hold** → AC3's 300 s bound fails.
4. **Residual gap (OPEN at implementation time):** the thrash cooldown was armed for this
   session at 10:39:36 and re-armed at 10:41:36 (`prefill_thrash_cooldown_started cooldown_s=600`),
   yet **zero** `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` lines appear for
   `01a177c6-…` in the whole file across 4 successive local dispatches (10:39:36 → 10:44:25),
   while `herdr-…` sessions are consistently skipped. The
   `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_remaining(_session_id, …)` gate in `provider.py` returned 0 for
   this session despite the armed key. Either the arm key differs from the check key
   (session-identity mismatch between router.py's arm and provider.py's check), or a
   dispatch path bypasses the local-branch gate — the AC1 deterministic test must pin this
   before choosing the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` is **not re-dispatched locally
   within the same request** (the detour goes to the next provider), **or** the
   re-dispatch is refused while the session's prefill-thrash cooldown is active — and the
   gate actually engages: asserted by a deterministic test with an injected clock and a
   stubbed local dispatcher (mirroring `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`) that
   would have caught this incident (i.e. it fails on the pre-fix behaviour of a fresh
   lease acquired 150 ms after the release). The test must also isolate why the
   2026-10-26 gate did not engage (arm-key vs check-key or bypass path) and assert the
   engaged skip.
2. After the cancellation the session's lease **and** `local_prefill_in_flight` marker are
   cleared before any retry, and the cancelled upstream prefill is cancelled (or proven
   dead) so `_extend_prefill_lease` cannot re-extend from a stale marker.
3. Any hold that does remain is bounded by <=300 s (the epic's 5 min bound): a regression
   test asserts release within 300 s simulated (no-progress watchdog must bound the record
   even when the session re-acquires).
4. `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure` over a >=24 h post-fix window
   reports `ac1.wedge_denials: 0` with no 300 s+ unproductive hold chain and
   `ac1.verdict_met: true`.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments,
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md`, and the prefill-recovery verification
   doc/README as applicable).
6. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The prefill deadline (120 s / 90 s default) is a deliberate
  "detour, don't kill" backstop; the fix must not push first-byte latency above
  `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds` and must not disable the thrash cooldown
  (`local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds`, rollback knob 0).
- The no-progress watchdog (180 s) and 10 s cleanup sweep cadence are production-bounded
  self-healing; the <=300 s bound must hold without weakening them.
- No-preemption lease semantics (same-session re-acquisition permitted) are load-bearing for
  legitimate long prefills; the fix must not break admission for genuine in-flight prefills.
- Fix scope lives in this item (the epic closes with this residual tracked; see Related work).

## Existing state

- `router.py`: on `prefill_deadline_exceeded` it arms the 600 s thrash cooldown, releases
  the lease + marker (`_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`), then the chain falls through —
  but the *next* local attempt (same request re-dispatch/retry) acquires a fresh lease;
  the thrash gate in `provider.py` did not engage for the affected session (see mechanism
  decision §4).
- `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` counts `active or expires_at > now` records as occupied;
  the sweep only deletes `not active AND expired` records outright, and the active-expired
  category extends records whose llama-server slot still reports processing — a wedged
  record can hold the pool until the no-progress watchdog.

## Desired change

- The post-deadline detour must be **terminal for local within that request** (no in-request
  local re-dispatch), and/or the thrash-cooldown gate must demonstrably engage for every
  local dispatch attempt (close the arm-key/check-key or bypass-path gap).
- Every local dispatch record must be released (or bounded) within <=300 s of its last
  progress, regardless of which path acquired it (deadline detour, same-session
  re-acquisition, active-expired sweep).
- `local_prefill_in_flight` must never outlive the dispatch it marks (no stale marker
  re-extension).

## Risks, assumptions and failure modes

- **Assumption:** the deployed llama-server's first byte genuinely arrives with the SSE
  headers (the monitor's premise), so a 120 s deadline miss means no client-visible byte —
  supported by 0 `Stream started: provider=local` lines for the session in the window.
- **Risk — over-correction:** making the deadline detour terminal for local could deny
  local to a session whose next *legitimate* request would have prefilled warm; mitigated by
  the existing 600 s cooldown already having this intent, and by clearing the cooldown on a
  successful local first byte.
- **Risk — masking the gate gap:** capping renewals only (the LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0 shape)
  bounds the hold but leaves the un-engaged thrash gate; AC1 must assert the gate engages.
- **Failure mode to test:** stale `local_prefill_in_flight` marker re-extending a record
  whose upstream is dead (`in_flight=True` extensions resumed after the release).
- **Scope-creep risk:** lease fairness (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0) and the 115 s second-slot
  residual (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) overlap this evidence; record any such work as linked
  items, do not absorb it here.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — local re-dispatch / slot-retry path after a deadline
  cancellation; thrash-cooldown routing gate (`_prefill_thrash_cooldown_remaining`),
  `_dispatch_local` call sites
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — deadline arm/release sequence
  (`prefill_deadline_exceeded`, `_record_prefill_thrash_cooldown`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`), `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` caller
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_extend_lease_during_prefill`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`, `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch`, `_watchdog_no_progress`,
  `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_*`, `_dispatch_lease_key`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` — deterministic injected-clock/stub harness
  to extend for the re-dispatch assertion
- `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` — AC4 measurement (`ac1.wedge_denials`,
  hold-chain accounting in `measure_wedge_denials`)

## Related work

- **LP-0MVKN9IRP003XJH6** — epic "Wedged prefill lease loop holds the local dispatch gate
  ~4 h" (completed/in_review); epic AC1 is the <=5 min bound this item enforces. The
  producer removed the epic's `depends-on` edge so the epic can advance: the epic closes
  with this residual tracked here (blocking edges on this item: none).
- **LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0** — Lease fairness (cap consecutive prefill-lease renewals); same
  log evidence; producer decided the epic closes with this residual tracked here, and the
  fix *may* land there instead only if the cooldown/lease cap also covers the in-request
  re-dispatch (AC1 allows either mechanism; otherwise fix here and note the overlap).
- **LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I** — 115 s/24 h second-slot residual (separate admission-shape
  residual; not to be conflated).
- **LP-0MU498TWH008DBCI** — Contention queue ignores prefill-saturated dispatches
  (completed; related queue behaviour).
- **LP-0MRB29PP60012UYF** — Stale local dispatch lease blocks subsequent requests
  (completed; prior stale-lease fix lineage).
- **LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2** — AC3 re-judgement that surfaced this residual
  (24 h window 2026-10-25 21:19 → 2026-10-26 21:19).

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q (producer, via description): "Which mechanism holds the gate — (a) the same request's
  local re-dispatch acquiring a fresh record, or (b) a differently-keyed release?"
  — Answer (intake, from log `proxy.log.2026-10-26_131429` + code read): **(a)** confirmed;
  (b) refuted (see Mechanism decision). Source: `[local] POST` 147–150 ms after each
  `lease_released`; `lease_extended_during_prefill in_flight=True` resuming 10 s after the
  release proves a fresh active record (the extension path only mutates an existing active
  record); watchdog release at 10:47:33 = 10:44:25 acquisition + 180 s + 10 s sweep.
- Q (implement comment): "the release line carries `endpoint=http://localhost:8080`, the
  extension path passes its own endpoint argument — is endpoint-key normalisation the
  defect?" — Answer (intake): no. `_dispatch_lease_key` does **not** normalise
  (`localhost:8080` vs `192.168.0.199:8000` are distinct keys), but the 10:41:46 post-release
  extension proves a live record under the extension path's key, and the release path only
  logs `lease_released` when it removed a record — so the record that wedged was acquired
  after the release, not left behind by a wrong-key release. The endpoint mismatch on the
  release line remains worth a defensive check (key-form consistency) at implementation time.
- Q (OPEN QUESTION — implementation must answer before choosing the fix): why did the
  600 s thrash cooldown armed at 10:39:36/10:41:36 for `01a177c6-…` fail to produce a
  single `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` across 4 successive local
  dispatches (10:39:36 → 10:44:25), while `herdr-…` sessions were consistently skipped?
  — Answer: **_not yet determined_**. Hypotheses to test with the AC1 injected-clock harness:
  (i) session-id mismatch between router.py's arm key (`session.session_id`) and
  provider.py's check key (`_session_id`, raw `x-session-id`/`session_id` header); or
  (ii) a local dispatch path that bypasses provider.py's local-branch gate.
  **Recommended (advisory):** treat the gate engagement as load-bearing — assert it in the
  deterministic test and fix whichever arm/check or bypass gap the test surfaces, rather
  than only capping renewals (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0-style), so AC1 holds for any path.
  Idempotence note: re-running intake must not duplicate this appendix entry.

Certify that the pinned 24 h window `2026-10-26T21:02:00Z → 2026-10-27T21:02:00Z`
is restart-free and that every precondition of the AC4 measurement is attested

window (new window = latest restart + 24 h, both windows recorded) and
invalidates this certification; the parent is retitled/re-pinned before
re-running. This child never yields PASS on a window containing a restart.

- **AC1 — Preconditions attested before measuring.** The result records: the

- **AC2 — Window pinned and restart-free.** The window is

  process is the deployed code), and both target changes are confirmed present

## Goal

Implement Option D's early abort: when the measured `prompt_progress` shows a dispatch is actually re-prefilling far more than admission priced, release the local lease early, log `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=measured_cache_deficit`, and detour to remote — wasting seconds instead of 120 s. Wire the pure decision from F3 into `proxy_to_local`'s reframed stream loop, driven by the capture from F2, behind a documented, rolled-back-able config knob.

## Background

Parent `LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27` AC2/AC3. The admission ladder stays byte-for-byte identical (Option A rejected — see parent "Design decision"). The abort fires at the first progress event that satisfies the F3 decision, at which point only a few hundred tokens of prefill have been wasted (the initial 0% event already carries the final `cache`).

## Acceptance Criteria

# Tune idle-admit eligibility to prefill feasibility (measured 0/31 conversion)

Discovered from: LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB (lease-gate decision item) — the AC5
tuning follow-up for LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the idle-admission override (`server.local_idle_admit_enabled`)
to admit only requests the local backend can prefill to first byte inside
`local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / the ETA-guard queue budget, so the override
no longer spends GPU time on doomed prefills with zero served responses.

## Measured evidence (window 2026-10-22 21:48:05 → 2026-10-23 21:48:05)

31 `routing_idle_admit` events, **0 conversions** (0/31 local first bytes):

- 22 dispatched to a local slot and cancelled at `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
  (90 s deadline in force at the time; `lease_extended_during_prefill ...
  progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` → no observable prefill progress
  before the deadline), then detoured remote.
- 9 rejected on arrival by the ETA admission guard
  (`local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct`,
  projected prefill 63–362 s vs the 60 s contention-queue budget).
- 0 refused by the `local_lease_active` gate; 0 first bytes.

Admitted prompt sizes 39–119 K cold tokens; window-wide `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
totalled 482 (= ~90 s per slot per abort). The after window was ~2× busier than
the before window (large_context_bypass 1,790 → 3,702; remote fallbacks 6,953 →
12,888), so this is a heavy-load measurement; the mechanism (admit → ETA-refuse
or deadline-abort) is load-independent.

Machine artifact: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`.

## Scope (candidate mechanisms to evaluate with the evidence)

- Prompt-size / projected-prefill eligibility **at admit time**: refuse the
  idle admit (keep the economic remote fallback) when `evaluate_admission`
  prices projected prefill beyond the deadline or the ETA guard would reject —
  i.e. make the override's admitted verdict consistent with the guard's
  (LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 AC3c already consults the guard; measure whether the
  dispatched-and-cancelled residue remains because the guard's calibrated
  refusal and the deadline disagree).
- Priority gating: only admit below a `high`-priority tier if interactive
  latency risk is unacceptable.
- Only if the 0-conversion persists after eligibility: reconsider the
  prefill-aware idle clock (option 5 of LP-0MVK16GME007EYUW) — the measured
  window had **zero** silent-prefill refusals, so this is the fallback, not
  the primary fix.
- Explicitly NOT in scope: preempting foreign dispatch leases — rejected in
  LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB (option 1 decision); do not reopen without new evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The override's admit decision is priced against projected prefill
   feasibility (ETA-guard budget + prefill deadline) and the measured
   0/31-conversion outcome is used as the regression signal: after the change,
   an equivalent window must show idle-admitted dispatches either converting
   to a first byte or being refused **before** dispatch (no
   `prefill_deadline_exceeded` on an idle-admitted session).
2. The fix is fail-safe: it can only refuse admissions the current code
   admits — it can never admit a request the guard or deadline refuses today.
3. Any new knob is config-read at dispatch time / hot-reloadable
   (`POST /admin/reload-config`), default preserves today's behaviour until
   the tuning demonstrates improvement (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC4).
4. Unit tests cover: admit-eligibility refusal on projected prefill beyond
   the deadline; the unchanged `context_too_large` cap; a calibrated vs
   uncalibrated (fail-open) bucket; and that the lease gate is untouched.
5. Docs: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` knob
   comments and `proxy/README.md` updated; decision on the flag recorded on
   LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF (window outcome was `measure`/`tune`, not
   `enable_by_default`).

## Related work

- LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB — parent decision (option 1: lease gate unchanged).
- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — parent measurement (window AC1–AC4 of record).
- LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J — ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review
  (budget/deadline re-derivation).
- LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I — residual deadline evictions with zero prefill progress.
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 / LP-0MVKUKEU80022C3U — guard/deadline bounds the
  override already consults.

`_note_local_fallback_reason()` is called on the router-skip / queue / direct-admission
